canonical_fact: A work package bundles authorization material, a work context and one or more work items for execution on a core.
misconceptions: A work package is equivalent to a JAM block.

relations.statement: A work package contains one or more work items.
A work package carries the authorization token used by its authorizer.
A work package carries the context that anchors historical inputs and prerequisites.

title: Work package

canonical_fact: A work item identifies a service and code hash, payload, Refine and Accumulate gas limits, imports, extrinsics and expected export count.
misconceptions: A work item always targets the same service as every other item in the package.
title: Work item

canonical_fact: A work context carries protocol context used to execute and validate work, including historical anchors and prerequisite information.
title: Work context

canonical_fact: A work package names the service whose historical preimage lookup hosts the authorization code used for that package.
title: Authorization code host

canonical_fact: A work package carries the hash of its authorization code, which must resolve through historical service lookup at the package's lookup anchor.
title: Authorization code hash

canonical_fact: Each work item carries a payload blob supplied as application-specific input to that service's Refine logic.
title: Work item payload

canonical_fact: Each work item specifies a gas limit bounding its in-core Refine execution.
title: Refine gas limit

canonical_fact: Each work item specifies a gas limit that later bounds the on-chain accumulation of that item's result.
title: Accumulate gas limit

canonical_fact: Work-package extrinsic data are blobs introduced alongside the package and committed by hash and length so Refine can receive them as external inputs.
title: Work-package extrinsic data

canonical_fact: A JAM export/import segment is a fixed-length 4104-octet data unit used for large-data communication between work packages through the availability system.
misconceptions: Segments are variable-length blobs with no protocol-defined fixed size.

relations.statement: Exported segments are instances of the fixed-size JAM segment type.
Imported segments are prior exported segments consumed by later work.

title: Data segment

canonical_fact: An exported segment is generated deterministically as a side effect of Refine execution and can later be imported by another work package.
misconceptions: Exported segments must already be included as raw data inside the work package before Refine runs.
title: Exported segment

canonical_fact: An imported segment is a segment exported by prior work and referenced through a segment-root/index or package-hash-derived reference so it can be fetched and justified.
misconceptions: An imported segment can be trusted solely because a validator returned the bytes.

relations.statement: Imported segments are verified against segment-root commitments using justification data.

title: Imported segment

canonical_fact: Imported data are committed through a Merkle root over exported segments, enabling a segment to be verified with an index and justification path.
title: Segment root

canonical_fact: A segment justification is Merkle proof data allowing a fetched imported segment to be checked against its committed segment root.
title: Segment justification

canonical_fact: A guarantor reconstructs imported segments by collecting enough erasure-coded chunks from distinct validators and then verifies them against their cryptographic commitments.
title: Imported-data reconstitution

canonical_fact: Guarantors construct an auditable work package containing the package plus needed extrinsic and imported data and concise proofs so auditors can re-execute work cheaply.
title: Auditable work package

canonical_fact: A work package may depend on prerequisite packages explicitly in its context or implicitly through imported segments referenced by exporting package hash.
title: Work-package dependency

canonical_fact: JAM limits the total number of work-package dependencies represented by prerequisites and package-hash imports.
title: Dependency limit

canonical_fact: The auditable work bundle includes a work package, imported and extrinsic data, payloads and authorization material subject to a protocol size bound.
title: Work bundle

canonical_fact: A work digest is the compact per-item result record carried in a work report, including service and code identity, payload hash, gas information, result and import, export and extrinsic counts.
title: Work digest

canonical_fact: A work report is the deterministic report produced from an authorized work package after Refine execution, containing its context, core and authorizer information, availability specification and work digests.
misconceptions: A work report directly mutates service storage when it is guaranteed.

relations.statement: A work report contains work digests for its constituent work items.
Validators sign guarantees over work reports before they enter the on-chain availability pipeline.

title: Work report

canonical_fact: A work report includes an availability specification committing to the work package and the data needed to make it available for later validators and auditors.

relations.statement: The availability specification commits to package data whose availability validators later assure.

title: Availability specification

canonical_fact: Refinement is the in-core execution process that validates package inputs and runs each work item's service Refine code to produce work digests and exported segments.
misconceptions: Refinement is the stage that commits arbitrary service storage changes directly into JAM state.
Refinement occurs only after accumulation has already changed state.

relations.statement: Refinement invokes each work item’s service Refine entry point.
The output of successful package refinement is summarized in a work report.

title: Refinement

canonical_fact: A Refine invocation may produce either a blob result or a defined work-execution error; the resulting outcome is captured in the work digest.
title: Work execution error

canonical_fact: Work packages are cryptographically hashed so reports, dependencies and imported-data references can identify the exact package involved.
title: Work-package hash
